title: AntiGem, a gem that *defies gravity*
tagline: A full coding environment, light enough to carry in your pocket.
description: An AI coding workspace for Android. Antigravity, Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex agents, a real Linux terminal, a code editor and a browser the agent can control, all in one app. Written from scratch in Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, with a Go bridge that supervises every agent.

features.title: Agents that actually code
features.text: Streaming replies, tool approvals, plans, subagents and diffs, parsed from each CLI's structured output. Not terminal scraping.

features.title: A real Linux, no root
features.text: Termux-based environment with apt, Python, Node, Go and Git at native speed. No root, no proot.

features.title: A browser the agent drives
features.text: Built-in browser plus Browser, Terminal, Android, Notes and Theme MCPs, one tap away for every agent.

features.title: Jarvis voice mode
features.text: Hand over a whole task by voice. It tells you when it's done, stuck, or needs your approval, even with the screen off.

features.title: Phone ⇄ PC
features.text: Pair with AntiGem for VS Code over SSH + SPAKE2. Same chats on both screens, files copy across.

features.title: Plugin SDK
features.text: Plugins add MCP tools and skills, running in an extension host that implements much of the Chrome extension API.

features.title: Build Android apps on Android
features.text: Kotlin/Compose, Flutter and React Native builds on the phone itself, driven by the agent.

features.title: Server mode
features.text: Move the bridge and agents to your VPS over an SSH tunnel. The phone becomes the screen.

orbit.title: The AntiGem *universe*
orbit.text: One app grew into a small ecosystem in under three months. Tap a satellite.

center.name: AntiGem
center.description: The Android app: Compose UI, terminal, editor, browser, MCP servers, Jarvis, and the Go bridge (agy_ide_bridge) that starts and supervises every agent.

rings.name: VS Code Extension
rings.description: The same agents and chat UI in a VS Code sidebar. Published on the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX. Connect phone makes your phone a second screen.

rings.name: Browser Bridge
rings.description: Chrome extension plus native messaging host that lets agents in VS Code drive your real browser: click, type, screenshot, run JS, read network logs.

rings.name: Plugins
rings.description: Official plugin repo: REA (reverse engineering), Android-dev toolchain and browser skills. The app checks it for updates in the background.

rings.name: Mini Apps
rings.description: An app store inside the app: HTML/JS mini apps with their own icon and Recents card, signed .agapp packages and a publish tool.

rings.name: Bootstrap Builder
rings.description: CI that builds custom Termux bootstraps for a different package name, solving hard-coded ELF interpreter and RUNPATH paths.

rings.name: Termux:X11
rings.description: AntiGem's build of Termux:X11, signed to share the com.termux UID so an XFCE or LXQt desktop runs inside AntiGem.

rings.name: Termux:API
rings.description: Signed companion app for hardware APIs (location, camera, sensors, SMS) over the shared UID.

rings.name: agy hub proxy
rings.description: Handles Antigravity's agy --hub feature to build a clean proxy in front of it.

architecture.title: How it *works*
architecture.text: The app never scrapes a terminal. A Go bridge speaks each agent's native protocol and streams structured events to the Compose UI.
